title: Structure of a C++ program: your first program

visuals.title: Match each part of a C++ program to its job

pairs.meaning: Brings in the tools for input and output
The place where the program starts

goal: After this you can write, read and explain a complete C++ program that prints a message.
warmup: Think of a rickshaw driver who only follows exact directions: 'Go straight, turn left, stop.' If you say the steps in the wrong order or skip one, he ends up somewhere else. A computer is the same: it follows your steps exactly, one by one, in the order you wrote them.
definition: A program is a list of instructions that a computer follows one after another. In C++, every program has a special part called main(). The computer always starts running from main().
howItWorks: Press Play to watch the computer move through the program. It starts at main(), runs each statement from top to bottom, prints text with cout, and stops at return 0.

sample.title: Hello UMT

explanation.text: Brings in the input/output library so we can use cout.
Lets us write cout instead of std::cout.
main() is where the program starts.
Prints the message. endl moves to a new line.
Returns 0 to say the program finished without problems.

steps.note: The computer finds main() and starts here.
cout sends the text Hello UMT to the screen, then endl moves to the next line.

worked.problem: Write a program that prints: Welcome to UMT, then on the same line the text CC111 after a tab, and then the word Done on a new line.
pseudocode: PRINT "Welcome to UMT" without a new line
PRINT a tab, then CC111, then a new line

flowchart TD

sample.title: Same line, tab and new line

explanation.text: No endl or \n here, so the next text continues on the same line.
\t inserts a tab; \n ends the line.
Prints Done on its own line.

variations.when: Print text and stay on the same line
Print text and move to a new line
Another way to move to a new line

mistakes.error: 'Cout' was not declared in this scope (C++ is case-sensitive)

examTips: Every statement ends with a semicolon (;).
C++ is case-sensitive: main is not Main.
#include <iostream> is needed for cout and cin.
romanSummary: Program computer ko steps batata hai, jo wo ek ek karke chalata hai.
Har C++ program main() se shuru hota hai.
cout screen par likhne ke liye use hota hai.
Har statement ke end par semicolon (;) lagana zaroori hai.

practice.prompt: Fill in the blank: every C++ program starts running from the function called ______.
practice.hint: It is the function with int in front.
practice.explanation: The computer always starts at main().

practice.hint: Look at the end of the first line.
practice.explanation: Every statement must end with a semicolon.

practice.prompt: Write a program that prints your name on one line and your roll number on the next line.
practice.hint: Use two cout statements with endl.
practice.explanation: Each cout prints one line; endl ends the line.

practice.hint: Only endl or \n starts a new line.
practice.explanation: A and B are on the same line because there is no newline between them. endl moves to the next line, so C is on line 2.

practice.prompt: Which header file is needed to use cout?
practice.hint: It has the word stream for input and output.

practice.answer: The closing brace } of main() is missing at the end.
practice.hint: Count the opening and closing braces.
practice.explanation: Every { needs a matching }. The compiler reports that it expected a } at the end of the input.

quiz.prompt: Where does a C++ program start running?
options: At the first line of the file
quiz.hint: One special function is the entry point.
quiz.explanation: The computer always begins execution at main().

quiz.prompt: Which symbol ends a C++ statement?
quiz.hint: Think of the full stop of a C++ sentence.

quiz.explanation: C++ is case-sensitive, so Cout is not the same as cout.
